title: Saucy Moroccan Haloumi and Beans
subtitle: with Herb Bread Dippers
description: Like your beans saucy? We certainly do! And we love them even more when they're topped with haloumi, laced with fragrant Moroccan spices and served with herby garlic bread for mopping up the sauce.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Cut the capsicum into 2cm chunks. Finely chop the parsley leaves and stems, keeping them separate. Drain and rinse the beans. Cut the haloumi into 1cm-thick slices. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves.

Cook capsicum and spices: Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium deep ovenproof frypan (see Make it yours) over medium heat. Cook the capsicum, stirring, for 3 mins or until softened. Add the parsley stems, Moroccan seasoning and 1 tbs tomato sauce and cook, stirring, for 30 secs.

Simmer beans: Add the beans, half the tomatoes, ½ tsp sugar and 180ml (¾ cup) boiling water to the pan and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 mins or until slightly thickened.

Prep bread dippers: Meanwhile, preheat the grill to high. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the bread rolls in half and put, cut side up, on the lined tray. Combine the garlic, half the parsley leaves and 3 tsp olive oil in a bowl. Brush the mixture over the cut sides of the rolls.

Grill and serve up: Remove the pan from the heat and arrange the haloumi on top of the bean mixture. Put the pan on the top oven shelf and the rolls underneath. Grill for 7-9 mins until the haloumi is golden and the rolls are crusty. Scatter the remaining parsley over the beans and haloumi. Serve with the dippers and enjoy!

Make it yours: If you don't have an ovenproof pan, simply transfer the bean mixture to an ovenproof dish before topping with haloumi and grilling. And while this is a perfect dish to serve in the middle of the table, you might prefer to divide the beans among 2 individual ovenproof dishes before grilling – no need to share!
